sentences.text: This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred by the petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 17.03.2025 passed by respondent No.1 whereby the appeal preferred by him against the order passed by respondent No.2 suspending his license has been dismissed.
02. On the basis of an inspection conducted at petitioner's premises, samples of confectionery items were prepared and Form 5A were taken.
Certain irregularities were found which were in violation of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The license of the petitioner was suspended and the Designated Officer passed an order on 23.01.2025.
The same was challenged by the petitioner by preferring an appeal which has also been dismissed by the impugned order.

03. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the samples which were sent to the State Food Laboratory for analysis in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:8449 2 WP-10596-2025 report have been stated to be confirming to the norms and were declared fit for human consumption hence the appeal preferred by the petitioner ought to have been allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State has pointed out that the fact of receipt of the lab reports has not been brought to the notice of the appellate authority by any of the parties which hence deserves to be directed to reconsider the matter.

05. The aforesaid contention is reasonable hence the order dated 17.03.2025 (Annexure P/1) passed by respondent No.1 is quashed and the appeal preferred by the petitioner before him is restored to its original number and shall be decided by him afresh by taking into consideration the reports of the food laboratory of samples taken from petitioner's premises.
06. With the aforesaid direction, the petition stands disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Tirupati Bakers And Confectioners ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73208296/
